# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41232%2E3422442%2EAMRLcr)
Peter,
I’m taking the debate stage again tonight, and I want to be clear about what I’m showing up to fight for: _lowering costs for working families and Californians._
That includes single-payer health care, free child care, tuition-free public college, less expensive housing. And this is just the baseline.
Because right now, Californians are getting crushed—rent, groceries, child care, health care—everything going up, and too many politicians are okay with the status quo.
Last debate, I called it like I saw it: when a self-funded billionaire is in the race, when Big Oil money is backing candidates, when Republicans are bringing Trump’s agenda to California, working people don’t come first.
**_Tonight, I’m ready to show voters again exactly who I’m fighting for—and who I’m fighting against._ And I’m ready to keep holding my opponents accountable and fighting for the same values I always have on stage.**
A lot of people will be tuning in, but we need to make sure that my message reaches _even more Californians_ after I step off stage and while people are still paying attention.
That means having the resources to meet voters wherever they are, and I need grassroots supporters to step up now to ensure we have them.
**[If you’re able, can you chip in $5 today to help us keep spreading our message before and after tonight’s debate?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260428_1_ak.qoa5JQ&refcode=em20260428-41232&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41232%2E3422442%2EAMRLcr)**

Katie

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | You don't get invited to the New York Stock Exchange with a prototype. subject: I'm endorsing Sam Forstag
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
When I was a bartender, I relied on tips to pay the bills. I know the urgent and daily stresses of working class people because I have lived them. And these experiences have made me a better member of Congress.
Today, I’m proud to let you know that **I am endorsing someone who understands this same struggle, Sam Forstag in MT-01**.
Sam is a smokejumper — a firefighter who parachutes out of planes to battle wildfires — and a union leader. He knows what it’s like to work two or three jobs at a time just to pay the bills.
I first met Sam last year on our Fighting Oligarchy Tour with Senator Sanders. He’s been on the frontlines of some of our most critical battles, fighting back against DOGE cuts and layoffs of Montana workers. I know he will be a force for working people in Congress.
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260428-forstag.etYxbz&refcode=em20260428-11280-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=11280%2E2526796%2E_ntyY8)
But big corporations, lobbyists, and the ultra wealthy are going to do everything they can to stop fighters like Sam. They’ve already committed major money toward winning this district.
Just like me and so many other progressive brawlers, Sam doesn’t take a dime of corporate PAC money. He isn’t independently wealthy. The only way he’s going to be able to win this race, is with the help of grassroots supporters like _you_.
[If you can, will you split a $5 contribution between each of our campaigns today? We need to keep the progressive movement growing strong in Congress — and that means we need fighters like Sam.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260428-forstag.etYxbz&refcode=em20260428-11280-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=11280%2E2526796%2E_ntyY8)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260428-forstag.etYxbz&refcode=em20260428-11280-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=11280%2E2526796%2E_ntyY8)**
Whether or not you can contribute today, thank you for standing with Sam and I in this fight for a better world.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

body:
This is a wake-up call we can’t ignore.
| Friend,
---
Republicans just LOST _more_ special elections – including one in Mar-a-Lago.
---
“Republicans are getting crushed in scores of state and local races, raising deep concerns about a deflated base refusing to show up to vote even in the most pro-Trump areas.” _-Axios_

**In response to the loss, some are accusing Republican voters of “abandoning” the party... even suggesting that you’ve become a Democrat!**
---
_But that response is dead wrong..._
---
Elected officials don’t have a “RIGHT” to serve. It’s a privilege given by voters like you.
---
The only rights I know about are **_YOUR_** _rights_ granted by God and protected by the Constitution.
---
The correct course of action is to _stop blaming voters_ , and start asking __WHY__.

**One stat shows that 39% of Republican voters have admitted they could sit out the midterm elections. If that happens, we’re in deep trouble.**

name: Sheriff Joe Arpaio
subject: The rioters walked. The cop who stopped them didn't.
body:
Dear Patriot,
They charged a cop with a felony for stopping a riot. I am not making this up.
They want to lock him away for using **non-lethal bean bag rounds** against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party.
I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed.
** [It has to stop — and I need your help to stop it.](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=2a1cb950dc8a4979b7946c87c54a31d4&_e=XHpUw_a8A7JwnxW7S6LgMIrAE39e6GS01oJFjuqWj3ImY21rrwUzrFGqUA_Xl1p_RfCC9nGZj00xQqtSpCJOtE5fRdnTB0IgK8zRQc3J9F2HL-rQ-jxRqobH-P7cl0K9O3_YFJthYhzJ0H27G9ZIqjGYPxyptB4OXPgua_sqP5ufTKtV5cKOv-kXvXDhQEZHX2D_Qeh9EC9ljMHGfCkj6WPxmJIDlju9P7dVzLCtUtTX6KFGjQJnjlCWhEkkOWmQtf-7lAB6Ve-Br7ZgWzdUXQg2tUyWLZT2TCZVDIzKJ-GhqUJxpRCOe07pGW_D610NF6wMwMAty4FylEiAZ8FT3PK5jnIupM7q2VFYQuei0JXFCWi05Adnl9YawXFszfquIA0RxTYrOTCXGypHYbjvIiMspAKBBlLDr-hTCLSBPPJEjXMte_KZmemUvZurE-c-) **
It was Memorial Day weekend, 2020. Hundreds of protesters flooded the streets of Austin. What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse.
On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused.
**Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway.**
Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife
When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence.
That's it. That's the "crime."
Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted.
This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets.

subject: John Roberts' endgame
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Knocking out this leg of the Voting Rights Act -- by weakening Section 2 -- would almost certainly reconstitute state legislatures, city councils, judicial districts, and every other type of political boundary in which racial minorities could be cut off from having a voice in their government.
This kind of change would silence untold numbers of voters and spiral our fight for voting rights back sixty years. RUSH $35 or more right now to help protect what the VRA stands for and defend our fundamental right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042826_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Mother Jones: Republican Justices Appear Poised to Destroy What’s Left of the Voting Rights Act [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042826_3&amount=25]
We'll hand this straight to Mother Jones, Team: " The Supreme Court, with its six-to-three Republican-appointed majority, appears ready to kneecap what remains of the Voting Rights Act’s protections for minority political representation. "
The descriptive language seems harsh, but the objective of these justices seems clear -- a complete dismantling of our seminal civil rights law . We've said it before and will say it again, but it's been clear long before the MAGA movement that Chief Justice Roberts has seen the removal of the VRA as one of his top goals for his time on the Court. It appears he may be on the cusp of succeeding.
During this week’s oral argument in Louisiana v. Callais , at least five conservative justices seemed ready to handicap the VRA so that it will no longer stop white majorities from locking racial minorities out of elected office through racial gerrymandering.
The consequences are simple to understand and grave for voter participation. The harder we make it to vote, the more politicians make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part. Needless to say, the less people who participate, the less our democracy and our government looks like the people it's supposed to represent.
Team: We have to spread the word about this case and the consequences of dismantling the Voting Rights Act. Fuel our work with $35 or whatever you can today and help us defend the right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042826_3&amount=35]

At issue in the case is Section 2 of the VRA, which requires that racial minorities have an equal opportunity to meaningfully participate in the electoral process. This provision has been used to strike down districting schemes and maps that prevented Black voters and other racial minorities from electing their preferred representatives. Since 1965, Section 2 has given people of color a seat at the table, from school boards to the halls of Congress. It appears this 60-year era is coming to an end.
“ Race is a part of redistricting always ,” Justice Sonia Sotomayor said, addressing the solicitor general from Louisiana, who was arguing against an existing map that had enabled the election of two Black members of Congress in his state. “ What you’re saying to us [is]...‘You can use [race] to help yourself achieve goals that reduce particular groups’ electoral participation, but you can’t use it to remedy that situation .’”
Striking down the last remnants of the Voting Rights Act is exactly why the Supreme Court held this case over from last year. Gutting Section 2 would take us backwards in time and allow racial gerrymandering to be a standard practice, silencing more voters. Just like the redistricting fights across the country, this is all about whether the party in power can choose their voters in order to stay in power in perpetuity.
We simply can't afford to go backwards like this. Will you chip in with $35 or more to help us fight back against these partisan efforts to silence voters? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=042826_3&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

# Newsom's billionaire tax has a dirty secret
California Governor Gavin Newsom is drawing increasing criticism for his proposed billionaire tax after a section on page 26 of the initiative came under scrutiny for **[allowing lawmakers to adjust the rules in the future.](https://substack.com/redirect/847d15e0-dd51-4564-a3a2-243fbb360344?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
* **Targeted Levy Details:** The California proposal would hit roughly two hundred residents whose net worth exceeds one billion dollars with a one-off five percent tax on excess amounts while permitting those payments to extend across several years for convenience.
* **Amendment Provision Highlighted:** However, page twenty six of the document empowers the state legislature to introduce changes after approval through a two thirds vote prompting fears of possible future broadening of the measure to cover more people.
* **Investor Issues Warning:** Venture Capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya called proposal an "Everyone Tax" in a viral post arguing the name distracts from how page twenty six allows government to transform it without needing fresh voter approval later on.
* **Defense and Reactions:** Supporters view the two thirds majority threshold plus the purpose requirement as solid safeguards against future expansion while some observers note similarities to early federal income tax rules that later grew dramatically in scale and rates.

Two teachers from Great Falls shaped everything I've done since. | [](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=93677969f8be4ce498af161cef234578&_e=Puor6HF4TwttQbKvIkG53vEOBnmzCDG88BJDDMilutX5pIIORRNHZJlOaDUQtDb7oK-nJq5lFaZZE3EYl-E-Fcr7KEk10oI_7qoj1nbNtOdoENIlaL9q9VvLFquo91L6XqXD9dvG2RH6TsNmJzNUSRf3VUyoyKaWJiN_4xzSPk6nlWtqPj3iAXot-6gUFnWNouOHgHpNEobxc5NMBozWhwBQYYBR2-6-_Jk2rWeCg1j31jW8_xei4IAGI0TPSxwF7YDRYoKkxFTVFHVj03XZ5BbpMk9wqtH1p4rnJ45P5oFUWhmTuuy2xlaPGLQ_Bh-UUe4gMBC66r95oqTWT1eVu8kqOjhUV5yUckgPh8se5bjaphCB4n8pF_LjiDS--AFlz1XroVfAVru-GmQsSfLLv5otRytLSQcr3IRtGIiu2gLymvK8xOY05V_RViog90mQi4CWVVoXJ-1nmSXYa035pYDUXN5FuxuNs8Q1KeIuq--nveSZWB1QcxcuXSlUxDzUpSukxv1SxohwMo859iDVaEFVoutLwViJ7lPCVbZF6oeVUHV_a-z4kFSEfs8LAGXI6KaCnEefkAMLQ2CxA_scBg5mI3MiF42twrFZ1jAfg-vBRs0ZZRWyrbj-R6H3uStl0GNyX5qDjsWQ7gCayY2lEog1hzKHwMbGIMYY97qBKFD25h6MI6WOH13JO6Pa2qNi)

Peter,

I want to tell you something about my parents.

My dad was a high school math teacher. My mom taught elementary school. They weren't famous. They weren't wealthy. But they showed up every single day for their students, their community, and their family.

They taught me three things that have never left me: work hard, keep your faith, and serve others.

_**By David Shuster**_
California's billionaires are freaking out.
Like most other obscenely wealthy Americans in this Trump era, the plutocrats have been bloated with paper wealth, fortified by legions of accountants, and possess a moral philosophy that rarely extends beyond their own reflection. They hold to the illusion that their fortunes are entirely their own. But, more than 1.5 million California voters have a different view and have now signed a petition pushing forward a ballot initiative that would impose a billionaire tax.
The California proposal is disarmingly simple: If voters approve the initiative this November, the state will impose a a one-time levy of roughly 5 percent on the swollen fortunes of those whose wealth has passed the billion-dollar mark. The proceeds will be directed largely towards health care, food assistance, and the assorted necessities of a functioning civilization.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40b266df-1388-4ee6-ac89-e62f7f98eb97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Naturally, the oligarchs oppose this measure and have reacted as though Attila were again at the gates.
The conservatives insist that the wealthy will flee California, as though the billionaires were a herd of delicate gazelles rather than the most resourceful economic animals ever to roam the continent. The conservatives warn that California's prosperity will evaporate overnight, that Silicon Valley will become a ghost town, that the sun itself may dim in protest.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40b266df-1388-4ee6-ac89-e62f7f98eb97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=195675153&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1Njc1MTUzLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzc0MTc2ODQsImV4cCI6MTc4MDAwOTY4NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.6j97jwPj-BlwuqK3gJrcm-_UB-FyhDiDKsXXtpf6mlQ)
The arguments would be comical if they were not so familiar: every modest attempt to pry a coin from the clenched fist of immense wealth is viewed, at least by the GOP, as the prelude to Armageddon.
But let's take a closer look at this hysteria with the cold eye of reason--or at least with something approaching it.
First, the tax is not an annual scourge but a one-time impost, a fleeting inconvenience to people whose balance sheets resemble the GDP of minor nations. The notion that such figures--who have already demonstrated a supernatural tolerance for risk, volatility, and the occasional market catastrophe--will be undone by a single 5 percent trim is, to put it delicately, bull shit.
Secondly, the revenue is not destined for some bacchanal of bureaucratic indulgence but for health care, education, and feeding the hungry --those dreary, unglamorous pillars upon which any halfway civilized society rests.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40b266df-1388-4ee6-ac89-e62f7f98eb97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=195675153&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1Njc1MTUzLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzc0MTc2ODQsImV4cCI6MTc4MDAwOTY4NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.6j97jwPj-BlwuqK3gJrcm-_UB-FyhDiDKsXXtpf6mlQ&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
If you believe, as most of us do, that that government exists to secure the general welfare, then this tax is not confiscation but good housekeeping.
Third--and here we approach the heart of the matter--is the opposition's moral argument. The billionaire, we are asked to believe, is a creature of such delicate genius that to tax such a person is to imperil the very engine of progress. Yet the same billionaire has flourished under a system of laws, courts, infrastructure, and public investments that he or she did not personally finance.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40b266df-1388-4ee6-ac89-e62f7f98eb97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The billionaires have driven on roads they did not pave, educated their workforce in schools they did not endow, and enforced contracts in courts they did not build. To suggest that a billionaire owes society absolutely nothing special is sickening. Relatedly, the objection to the tax seems not about economics but about theology. There is an old American capitalist superstition that great wealth is a sign of divine favor, and that to touch it--even lightly--is a species of blasphemy. Under this creed, the billionaire is not merely rich; the billionaire is consecrated. And the billionaire's fortune is sacrosanct.
Thankfully, California voters appear ready to commit a small heresy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40b266df-1388-4ee6-ac89-e62f7f98eb97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

To get on the fall ballot, the billionaire tax initiative required 875,000 signatures. It now has twice that many and counting. Because at least in California, and perhaps elsewhere, the public is not entirely enamored with oligarchy.
Sen. Bernie Sanders (I., Vt.) and Rep. Ro Khanna (D., Calif.) have embraced the California proposal and are pushing a federal billionaire tax as well. But that federal proposal is a column for a different day.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40b266df-1388-4ee6-ac89-e62f7f98eb97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

California, which is a trend setter for the rest of the nation, has taken the lead. And it should be noted that not all billionaires are against the proposal. Nvidia's Jensen Huang says he is "perfectly fine" with the proposed tax and recently encouraged other billionaires to move to California.
The state's billionaire tax, if approved, will come at a crucial time. The Medicaid cuts in the Trump/GOP tax and spending bill from 2025 will take effect after the midterm elections. In California, as in all other states, the "big, beautiful bill" will mean lost healthcare jobs in 2027, sicker residents, and higher premiums unless funding gaps are filled.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40b266df-1388-4ee6-ac89-e62f7f98eb97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=195675153&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1Njc1MTUzLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzc0MTc2ODQsImV4cCI6MTc4MDAwOTY4NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.6j97jwPj-BlwuqK3gJrcm-_UB-FyhDiDKsXXtpf6mlQ&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
Relatedly, the billionaire tax did not start as a statement about rising inequality. It gained traction when California lawmakers began debating ways of solving a huge and approaching Medicaid funding shortfall.
It is certainly possible that some billionaire fortunes will move out of the state, accountants will earn their keep, and the tax revenue will not usher in budgetary rainbows and unicorns. Public policy rarely achieves such dramatic results. But the choice before the California voter is not between perfection and ruin. It is between a state that asks something modest of its most fortunate citizens and one that asks nothing at all while public systems creak and falter.
In that contest, the sensible verdict is plain.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40b266df-1388-4ee6-ac89-e62f7f98eb97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Tax the billionaires--not because they are villains, nor because success is a crime, but because a society that cannot summon the nerve to do so is one that has mistaken wealth for wisdom and power for virtue. And as any halfway attentive observer of the American scene will tell you, that sort of thinking is the beginning of rot.
Californians, thankfully, seem ready to give their state budget a fresh start.
A [poll](https://substack.com/redirect/8f4dca07-c8d5-4592-bea2-da8e00c78fad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) published last month by the UC Berkeley Institute of Government Studies found 52% of California voters were inclined to vote for the billionaire tax, 33% opposed it, and 15% were undecided.
Bravo, California.
Let the fairness begin.
* * *
What's happening in California is the same fight we're in every day.
The predator class--the billionaires, the oligarchs, the people who treat paying their fair share as a personal insult--has been winning for forty years. They bought the press. They bought the politicians. They bought the courts. They want you tired, distracted, and quiet.
We're none of those things. And we're only here because _you_ fund this.

A billionaire tax just qualified for the November ballot -- and an Nvidia billionaire is already telling his friends to move to California. Shuster on the heresy of the year. | | and | Apr 28 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- By David Shuster California's billionaires are freaking out. Like most other obscenely wealthy Americans in this Trump era, the plutocrats have been bloated with paper wealth, fortified by legions of accountants, and possess a moral philosophy that rarely extends beyond their own reflection. They hold to the illusion that their fortunes are entirely their own. But, more than 1.5 million California voters have a different view and have now signed a petition pushing forward a ballot initiative that would impose a billionaire tax. The California proposal is disarmingly simple: If voters approve the initiative this November, the state will impose a a one-time levy of roughly 5 percent on the swollen fortunes of those whose wealth has passed the billion-dollar mark. The proceeds will be directed largely towards health care, food assistance, and the assorted necessities of a functioning civilization. | | ---|---|--- Naturally, the oligarchs oppose this measure and have reacted as though Attila were again at the gates. The conservatives insist that the wealthy will flee California, as though the billionaires were a herd of delicate gazelles rather than the most resourceful economic animals ever to roam the continent. The conservatives warn that California's prosperity will evaporate overnight, that Silicon Valley will become a ghost town, that the sun itself may dim in protest. | | ---|---|--- The arguments would be comical if they were not so familiar: every modest attempt to pry a coin from the clenched fist of immense wealth is viewed, at least by the GOP, as the prelude to Armageddon. But let's take a closer look at this hysteria with the cold eye of reason--or at least with something approaching it. First, the tax is not an annual scourge but a one-time impost, a fleeting inconvenience to people whose balance sheets resemble the GDP of minor nations. The notion that such figures--who have already demonstrated a supernatural tolerance for risk, volatility, and the occasional market catastrophe--will be undone by a single 5 percent trim is, to put it delicately, bull shit. Secondly, the revenue is not destined for some bacchanal of bureaucratic indulgence but for health care, education, and feeding the hungry --those dreary, unglamorous pillars upon which any halfway civilized society rests. | | ---|---|--- If you believe, as most of us do, that that government exists to secure the general welfare, then this tax is not confiscation but good housekeeping. Third--and here we approach the heart of the matter--is the opposition's moral argument. The billionaire, we are asked to believe, is a creature of such delicate genius that to tax such a person is to imperil the very engine of progress. Yet the same billionaire has flourished under a system of laws, courts, infrastructure, and public investments that he or she did not personally finance. | | ---|---|--- The billionaires have driven on roads they did not pave, educated their workforce in schools they did not endow, and enforced contracts in courts they did not build. To suggest that a billionaire owes society absolutely nothing special is sickening. Relatedly, the objection to the tax seems not about economics but about theology. There is an old American capitalist superstition that great wealth is a sign of divine favor, and that to touch it--even lightly--is a species of blasphemy. Under this creed, the billionaire is not merely rich; the billionaire is consecrated. And the billionaire's fortune is sacrosanct. Thankfully, California voters appear ready to commit a small heresy. | | ---|---|--- To get on the fall ballot, the billionaire tax initiative required 875,000 signatures. It now has twice that many and counting. Because at least in California, and perhaps elsewhere, the public is not entirely enamored with oligarchy. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I., Vt.) and Rep. Ro Khanna (D., Calif.) have embraced the California proposal and are pushing a federal billionaire tax as well. But that federal proposal is a column for a different day. | | ---|---|--- California, which is a trend setter for the rest of the nation, has taken the lead. And it should be noted that not all billionaires are against the proposal. Nvidia's Jensen Huang says he is "perfectly fine" with the proposed tax and recently encouraged other billionaires to move to California. The state's billionaire tax, if approved, will come at a crucial time. The Medicaid cuts in the Trump/GOP tax and spending bill from 2025 will take effect after the midterm elections. In California, as in all other states, the "big, beautiful bill" will mean lost healthcare jobs in 2027, sicker residents, and higher premiums unless funding gaps are filled. | | ---|---|--- Relatedly, the billionaire tax did not start as a statement about rising inequality. It gained traction when California lawmakers began debating ways of solving a huge and approaching Medicaid funding shortfall. It is certainly possible that some billionaire fortunes will move out of the state, accountants will earn their keep, and the tax revenue will not usher in budgetary rainbows and unicorns. Public policy rarely achieves such dramatic results. But the choice before the California voter is not between perfection and ruin. It is between a state that asks something modest of its most fortunate citizens and one that asks nothing at all while public systems creak and falter. In that contest, the sensible verdict is plain. | | ---|---|--- Tax the billionaires--not because they are villains, nor because success is a crime, but because a society that cannot summon the nerve to do so is one that has mistaken wealth for wisdom and power for virtue. And as any halfway attentive observer of the American scene will tell you, that sort of thinking is the beginning of rot. Californians, thankfully, seem ready to give their state budget a fresh start. A published last month by the UC Berkeley Institute of Government Studies found 52% of California voters were inclined to vote for the billionaire tax, 33% opposed it, and 15% were undecided. Bravo, California. Let the fairness begin. What's happening in California is the same fight we're in every day. The predator class--the billionaires, the oligarchs, the people who treat paying their fair share as a personal insult--has been winning for forty years. They bought the press. They bought the politicians. They bought the courts. They want you tired, distracted, and quiet. We're none of those things. And we're only here because you fund this. the most direct punch you can throw at the predator class from the comfort of your couch. Can't swing it? Every dollar you send us is a dollar that doesn't have to come from a sponsor we'd be ashamed of, an advertiser who'd want a quieter version of us, or a billionaire who'd want us silenced. Tax the billionaires. Fund the press they can't buy. Same fight. -- Cliff You're currently a free subscriber to . subject: Citizenship, not mass deportation
body:
We’re asking Congress to stop funding mass deportation and create a viable path to citizenship. | | | Peter,
Ahead of the Senate’s recent vote-a-rama, United We Dream joined more than 160 other organizations in a letter urging lawmakers to reject funneling $140 billion _more_ taxpayer dollars into deadly immigration enforcement operations for the next three years, without going through the regular appropriations process. We called for a pathway to citizenship as the economically smart and morally just solution Americans overwhelmingly support. Instead of spending billions on the current mass deportation and detention policies that are tearing the fabric of this nation to shreds — ripping teachers out of classrooms, disappearing servicemembers’ spouses, separating families, raiding church pews, and shuttering small businesses — we’re asking Congress to finally resolve the issue by creating a viable path to citizenship. Creating an opportunity for immigrants to come forward, pass a background check, and apply for lawful permanent residency, ultimately becoming naturalized citizens, is the solution policymakers should focus on. An agenda for an affirmative vision calls for bold, permanent protections that are immune to policy whiplash. **Citizenship is the gold standard for protection for those who already call America home**. Together we can achieve that, and build a vibrant and diverse economy that works for all, not just the billionaires and those cruelly profiting from the pain and suffering of immigrants. **[Your contribution to United We Dream will help us continue working toward the goal of safety, dignity, and citizenship for our immigrant communities.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIdicNPDEjB8U81Sf47SIVAIJcGdce1WPoM-U456g84PoqF_Cy4jScVojz1q1v2y8U8FtdZX4Yb56A9ofznf1KTO0jCcCa5_rKCUhcCCog8PiCcKbss8oc5FJQUbZujVkBS2IRcpyyA0MS-sN5miShsi3sQaON28JzMBeHMF-PsvdHlO4piyl4SbO_umzXptihS4WO_36qGhRTaaB8RTScY0OU1eHMJYWWZNU9w9XZxrZt2AX8orC3LTUZxxaHgK7_Q8tB83yjxXMNR2HRI-q6kPsTmtfoktbdR-RzeXYtIT42i0tWalNO5lCYAJ0i-xLSMCEcx0Pl2A5RFY96sMYWqYVAPe-0TAWqAB4vBXeHrrY2vDaEkGfZF7Q1g6Pa4pZDQHQQbRy6ox1gmwHAwH6zQ/4q6/Uvwy96_0SZGQzFKogWKDlQ/h0/h001.r9OfgLEO3gfDu9YfRJpQETSYHCUS8_ccaOEdpjBvS-s)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [express donate: $10](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIdicNPDEjB8U81Sf47SIVAIJcGdce1WPoM-U456g84PoqF_Cy4jScVojz1q1v2y8U8FtdZX4Yb56A9ofznf1KYkvQONPbAkJzuE6CkHCYFm7i8s6Fh2pxU9PR6E1n2t6MOWpwMs_xbb89LrmKKkh1DGy78X-h4OF86QoG57RZGJ-lplclu4Tm80Uk1NBNy9ayrGovyBipM0lImMNs1Vn-URfPy5UvBA_BtC6fySZjgDR0FRaHa1oUTgoh4Q6bSLoHXMPVgvVtDkIUpcCdeLg1wjtNLe0DsvPwvsP1kOoesq6H1mvZouVyYUphmlDGdKBcjmv7lrnc67wT0F40md4PDFZYIpKIz3XK5NHW-dzfs8vRbm2-EsoPyn4oQXrcbNux0RWPF3UEKZx_KN1FoD1m_vZQcYv0R5QMcrgwEv3-7pIZwzFzqP3lXT1B7BDrc0g/4q6/Uvwy96_0SZGQzFKogWKDlQ/h1/h001.2ISce-Y44tjV_Q52grYynhVhn4gXiu6hIMus9Cnjc4k)

clean_body: We’re asking Congress to stop funding mass deportation and create a viable path to citizenship. | | | Peter, Ahead of the Senate’s recent vote-a-rama, United We Dream joined more than 160 other organizations in a letter urging lawmakers to reject funneling $140 billion more taxpayer dollars into deadly immigration enforcement operations for the next three years, without going through the regular appropriations process. We called for a pathway to citizenship as the economically smart and morally just solution Americans overwhelmingly support. Instead of spending billions on the current mass deportation and detention policies that are tearing the fabric of this nation to shreds — ripping teachers out of classrooms, disappearing servicemembers’ spouses, separating families, raiding church pews, and shuttering small businesses — we’re asking Congress to finally resolve the issue by creating a viable path to citizenship. Creating an opportunity for immigrants to come forward, pass a background check, and apply for lawful permanent residency, ultimately becoming naturalized citizens, is the solution policymakers should focus on. An agenda for an affirmative vision calls for bold, permanent protections that are immune to policy whiplash. Citizenship is the gold standard for protection for those who already call America home. Together we can achieve that, and build a vibrant and diverse economy that works for all, not just the billionaires and those cruelly profiting from the pain and suffering of immigrants. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | As immigrants and workers who power this country, we fight to shut down bills that only offer breadcrumbs and instead pass tangible, genuine, and popular solutions. Thank you for working to help us achieve that goal. — Aria, United We Dream Follow us on: | | | | |

| Peter,
By now you've surely heard about Calvin Duncan, the black man who taught himself law while in jail, got himself exonerated, and then ran for and won the race for the clerk of the Orleans Parish criminal court to reform the system that stole nearly 30 years of his life.
Rather than allow him to be sworn in, MAGA introduced legislation to eliminate his office altogether.
Now we come bearing the bad news we knew was coming, the Louisiana Legislature has passed SB 256 eliminating the office of the Orleans Parish Criminal Court -- all to stop Calvin Duncan from taking office.

## Book Launch: Trump 2.0 available NOW!
It's official!
My new book, _Trump 2.0,_ is out.
I want to thank all of you who preordered the book, pre-sales are critical to a book's success so your support is super helpful.
I'm excited for everyone to get the chance to read it, and learn just why Trump's second term is so consequential.
### Special invitation...
If you live in the DMV area, I'd like to invite you to a book event this Friday at the Kennedy Center--tickets are free and on sale now.
[Reserve your ticket HERE!](https://substack.com/redirect/6395c42c-e51c-4072-9902-a8dd67ccd561?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'll be talking with Larry O'Connor, along with special guests Chip Roy, Tim Burchette, Beth van Duyne, Rich McCormick, and Steve Scalise.
I had some great conversations at the RSC's new media day, and I can't wait to continue those at this Friday's event, with a VIP reception to follow.
[Buy VIP tickets HERE!](https://substack.com/redirect/e85372d2-d480-4076-97f8-b70aff0891d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Reserve tickets now, before the event fills up!
We'll be talking _Trump 2.0,_ and so much more.
The book covers a lot of ground, from NATO to MAHA, education reform to immigration.
I explain how President Trump has been preparing for this for four years--and what's coming next after his second term.
Don't take my word for it though.
Here's a sneak peek from the book--President Trump's foreword:
There are few people who understand Trump 2.0 better than my former White House Press Secretary Sean Spicer. He has been with me since the beginning and never stopped fighting for the MAGA agenda.
If you want to understand the people, the policies, and the process of my second term in office, there is no better book to read.
If you want to understand why we are winning so much, this is the book for you.
Trump 2.0. isn't just another four years in office.
It's the beginning of a whole new era of American greatness.
[Order Trump 2.0 HERE!](https://substack.com/redirect/983c1afe-58f2-4f22-977b-50dc9fbca21c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm grateful for everyone's support that has gotten us to this launch.
And I can't wait to see many of you this Friday for the _Trump 2.0_ event at the Kennedy Center.
I hope you enjoy reading the book as much as I did writing it!

Peter,
Too many politicians are still clearly afraid to say that Democrats lost to Trump in 2024 because of their support for the genocide in Gaza.
Still, too many leaders refuse to confront what’s happening and call Gaza what it is—an ongoing genocide of Palestinians enabled by U.S. policy and military funding. And now that violence is spreading throughout the region—most notably in Lebanon and Iran—with the help of Donald Trump and the Republicans in Congress.
Even as Donald Trump escalates dangerous, extreme rhetoric and threatens entire populations abroad, establishment politicians keep circling back to the same big money donors and the same defense of the status quo.

AIPAC and other MAGA-backed political networks are pouring money into races across this country to protect politicians who refuse to challenge U.S. support for Netanyahu’s genocide.
It’s why I’ve been targeted. Last cycle, they spent $15 million trying to take me down. And they’ve already started pouring money into my opponent’s campaign to try to silence me because I refuse to stay silent.
I’ve always stood with the people of Gaza. I’ve called for an end to U.S. support for and complicity in the genocide. And I’m not backing down now.
Meanwhile, my opponent continues to benefit from donors and PACs that reward silence instead of courage.
We are less than four months from our primary, and we cannot afford to be outspent and outmaneuvered again. This campaign is powered by people, not corporations, not AIPAC-linked donors, not special interests.

Jon

subject: URGENT: Trump puts nearly 700,000 acres of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge up for auction
body:
We need your help.

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM2Njc4MTcS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQ0MDM4ODkyMgS2&mt=1&rt=0).

* * *
---
| | | | DEVELOPING... Trump’s Department of the Interior has announced it will auction off nearly _**700,000 acres**_**in the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge for oil and gas drilling.**
---
| | **The environmental movement has to act. **
---
| | [**_The best thing you can do right now to help? Renew your LCV membership today. $15 is all it takes >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/k_)
---
| | The Coastal Plain is the beating heart of the Arctic Refuge. It provides essential habitat for polar bears, millions of migratory birds, and the Porcupine caribou herd, which is critical to the culture and sustenance of the Gwich’in people.
---
| | For decades, the Gwich’in people have worked to protect their ancestral homelands from the long reach of the fossil fuel industry. Their work has meant _**there has never been drilling in these wetlands, tundra, and rivers._Ever_.**_
---
| | Here’s the thing: drilling here is not only bad economics — it’s reckless and wildly unpopular. Time and time again, when Trump feels serious pressure, he backs down. And if Trump doesn’t back down, we need to make sure the oil companies feel the heat too.
---
| | Your renewed membership will power our work to **defend the Arctic Refuge** from reckless oil and gas drilling. It will mobilize support for **clean, sustainable energy solutions**. And it will push for policies that actually **address the real energy crisis** we’re facing right now.
---
| | **We have to keep the pressure up, Peter.**[**Please, renew your membership for $15 today to power our work to protect the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge >>**](https://links.messages.lcv.)

| | Thank you for everything you do for people and our planet, Peter.

| | Sincerely,

If you have a minute, I want to share a bit about my personal life that you may not know yet.
I was raised by social justice warriors.
My dad marched for civil rights in Selma, Alabama, where he heard Martin Luther King Jr. preach. My mom, born and raised in the Philippines, spent years fighting for the restoration of democracy in her home country.
My parents had me while living and working in the Philippines as social justice missionaries. I was born when a dictator was rising to power and martial law was imminent.
It was critical to both of my parents that I grow up in a country with democracy, freedom, rule of law, and human and civil rights — and sadly it became clear to them that wasn’t the case in the Philippines. So they brought my family here, to California, when I was just two months old.
A short while later, my parents began working with the United Farm Workers of America, fighting for workers’ rights, fair pay, and shade and water breaks.
I would never have guessed as a young kid that I would grow up to serve as the Attorney General of California — but as long as I can remember, I’ve known that I wanted to fight for those most vulnerable to have a fair shot at the California Dream.
That’s why I do this work. I know, without a doubt, that the California Dream is alive and well because I’m living mine — and I’m committed to using every bit of platform and power I have to lift people up and fight for justice for all.
I’m up for re-election in November, and I want nothing more than to continue this fight.
California needs an Attorney General who will stand up to those who abuse their power — whether it’s corrupt politicians, corporate polluters, extremist groups trying to roll back our rights, or powerful interests that exploit workers, cheat consumers, and put profits ahead of people.
So I’m asking you for help: Will you donate to my re-election campaign before our April end-of-month deadline? Every single dollar we raise right now helps us build a stronger grassroots movement to protect our freedoms — and win in November. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]

| | To me, a budget's far more than lists and charts of numbers; it's a moral document — because what you choose to prioritize shows what you _really_ care about. Trump gave us some insight into his thought process earlier this month at a private lunch with his supporters where he told them, **"We can't take care of daycare. We're a big country. We're fighting wars. It's not possible for us to take care of daycare, Medicaid, Medicare, all these things."** He certainly showcased that callous mindset when he released his budget proposal. Here's a taste of the priorities in it:
* Removing funds for life-saving health research, disease prevention, and clean water
* Cutting yet _more_ money from FEMA and weather monitoring systems for wildfires, floods, hurricanes, you name it
* Ending HUD initiatives focused on growing our affordable housing supply
* Slashing billions more from public schools, youth vocational training, and college

All of this (and more cuts) to offset the massive hike in military spending that Trump claims we need in the wake of the war he started with Iran. **Imagine that: drawing us into a conflict we never asked for, and then forcing the American people to play a cruel zero-sum game.** Well, I refuse to play that game. I stand for a _fair_ budget — one that doesn't force us to choose between which essential programs for healthcare, education, or working families we can save. clean_body: | | | | To me, a budget's far more than lists and charts of numbers; it's a moral document — because what you choose to prioritize shows what you really care about. Trump gave us some insight into his thought process earlier this month at a private lunch with his supporters where he told them, "We can't take care of daycare. We're a big country. We're fighting wars. It's not possible for us to take care of daycare, Medicaid, Medicare, all these things." He certainly showcased that callous mindset when he released his budget proposal. Here's a taste of the priorities in it: Removing funds for life-saving health research, disease prevention, and clean water Cutting yet more money from FEMA and weather monitoring systems for wildfires, floods, hurricanes, you name it Ending HUD initiatives focused on growing our affordable housing supply Slashing billions more from public schools, youth vocational training, and college All of this (and more cuts) to offset the massive hike in military spending that Trump claims we need in the wake of the war he started with Iran. Imagine that: drawing us into a conflict we never asked for, and then forcing the American people to play a cruel zero-sum game. Well, I refuse to play that game. I stand for a fair budget — one that doesn't force us to choose between which essential programs for healthcare, education, or working families we can save. = = Onward, Ron | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Ron Wyden instantly: | = | = | = | = ---|---|---|--- | | Paid for and authorized by Wyden for Senate. | This email was sent by Wyden for Senate P.O. Hi Peter, We’re now four weeks out from runoff election day. This race matters. An independently elected office of the executive branch, the Texas Attorney General is one of the most powerful positions in Texas government. The constitutional duty of the AG is pretty clear: represent the interests of the state in courts, and serve as a check against the abuse of power in the private sector and the public sector. This means upholding the rule of the law, preserving individual rights, preserving separation of powers, guarding against government overreach, and protecting people from predatory and anticompetitive behavior in the marketplace. Those haven’t been priorities for the Texas Attorney General over the last decade or so. The office – under current AG Ken Paxton and previously under Greg Abbott – has been pulled into an absurd sort of combative political theater, distracting and depriving resources from the work that we need the AG’s Office to do. Across Texas, people who don’t always agree on everything are agreeing on this: we need an Attorney General who gets the Office back to the serious work it was intended to do. As your Attorney General, I will use the power of the Office to defend our rights and freedoms, to make government work in service of the people, un-rig markets, uphold the rule of law, and preserve the Constitution. I’ve been on the front lines of every major Democratic fight in the Texas Senate, opposing bad policy while working across the aisle to pass more than 130 good bills. That balance matters, and so does the skill and judgment it takes to achieve it. And while we must insist that the Attorney General’s office not be used as a political tool, we must recognize that it operates in a highly charged political environment. It will require skill and judgment, honed through experience, to do the job right. clean_body: As Attorney General I’ll fight for your rights. To unsubscribe, | | Hi Peter, We’re now four weeks out from runoff election day. This race matters. An independently elected office of the executive branch, the Texas Attorney General is one of the most powerful positions in Texas government. The constitutional duty of the AG is pretty clear: represent the interests of the state in courts, and serve as a check against the abuse of power in the private sector and the public sector. This means upholding the rule of the law, preserving individual rights, preserving separation of powers, guarding against government overreach, and protecting people from predatory and anticompetitive behavior in the marketplace. Those haven’t been priorities for the Texas Attorney General over the last decade or so. The office – under current AG Ken Paxton and previously under Greg Abbott – has been pulled into an absurd sort of combative political theater, distracting and depriving resources from the work that we need the AG’s Office to do. Across Texas, people who don’t always agree on everything are agreeing on this: we need an Attorney General who gets the Office back to the serious work it was intended to do. As your Attorney General, I will use the power of the Office to defend our rights and freedoms, to make government work in service of the people, un-rig markets, uphold the rule of law, and preserve the Constitution. I’ve been on the front lines of every major Democratic fight in the Texas Senate, opposing bad policy while working across the aisle to pass more than 130 good bills. That balance matters, and so does the skill and judgment it takes to achieve it. And while we must insist that the Attorney General’s office not be used as a political tool, we must recognize that it operates in a highly charged political environment. Meet Wes.
He’s our lead organizer in the greater Austin area, helping our volunteers meet, register and stay in touch with voters at UT Austin, Austin Community College and traveling as far as San Antonio and San Marcos to help at colleges there.
Wes is tireless, committed and innovative, always trying new ways to improve our program and the number of voters we turn out. He’s also a student at UT Austin, giving him a direct connection to the young Texans who represent the margin of victory in close elections.
That’s critical — because when we take the time to personally connect with a student, get them on the voting rolls and help them through any questions or concerns they have about voting (and give them a nudge at election time) they are more than twice as likely to vote as their peers.
Like all of our organizers, we pay Wes a living wage, provide healthcare insurance and cover his travel expenses as he moves across Central Texas to reach these important voters.

He’s also a student at UT Austin, giving him a direct connection to the young Texans who represent the margin of victory in close elections. That’s critical — because when we take the time to personally connect with a student, get them on the voting rolls and help them through any questions or concerns they have about voting (and give them a nudge at election time) they are more than twice as likely to vote as their peers. Like all of our organizers, we pay Wes a living wage, provide healthcare insurance and cover his travel expenses as he moves across Central Texas to reach these important voters. ⁃ PXP

body:
Dear Patriot,
They charged a cop with a felony for stopping a riot. I am not making this up.
They want to lock him away for using **non-lethal bean bag rounds** against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party.
I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed.
** [It has to stop — and I need your help to stop it.](http://links.standingstrongamerica.com/u/click?_t=29c3b6e742c849fabbcc130432510e66&_m=501b86d56a8a40c4b24ff1af0b58b11d&_e=wxlI0S6vVf-SqOfeTtl_noJnYHyyRha0zLIjN6UsIWeDPTAfvj3TFBy6eqSL5H-ve6NP_ys0HVGPL2gMN59WYvAUN9UjOiZZNbS4_hrpmsXz6bLShUzVR-N8sK8oHOkDh3MJRhq_J7mmQbD1SGscaGQzqVDEnXmNHw_GZT8JihZ9RtqdbB1k8dgNYurFLynWhKWXzZzwtFZyPI8Ev_rMBG4170DvMGIk0fOh43XeYf-wzBhHwg2rJfX18EMRjl0r8ZbUAdqvKLSbCPEkRoLudIUI-6Y1_KTXxNuCWft4Jrze5YyMNi_vdzgjHkWFreebvsmhmlvobMxEkqWJ6xWnfNc-AOmlz9mzvbueql6QI1KPNOoWMveAQy5kVEh_sFSZI4bKzggJwRLv12YZUx7Er_GD9PDVhJi0-rSd957jEtWklRKxIqxobjvMtiA0ulqR) **
It was Memorial Day weekend, 2020. Hundreds of protesters flooded the streets of Austin. What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse.
On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused.
**Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway.**
Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife
When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence.
That's it. That's the "crime."
Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted.
This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets.
And Jeff Teng is paying the price. His career is on hold. His future is uncertain. His trial has been delayed again and again — meaning this family has been living under this cloud for _years_ with no end in sight.

#
Peter —
First and foremost, I want to thank everyone who has joined this grassroots movement. It is unlike anything I’ve ever experienced. We are in a strong position to take back Texas because there are hundreds of thousands of us working together to win this fight.
And while I truly wish we did not have to send a single fundraising email, I have no choice with our April fundraising deadline approaching and millions of dollars pouring into Texas to prop up my Republican opponents.
The truth is, our fundraising has been slower than we expected this month. With Republicans in a bruising runoff, we have the advantage of a head start — but only if we have the resources to organize and scale up across Texas.
Early money has an outsized impact on what is possible. The money we raise today will determine whether or not we can bring people over to our side and turn out new voters who will decide this race in November.
Waiting until after the runoff is not an option when billionaire and corporate mega-donors are trying to buy this race. I wish I didn’t have to ask you, but messages like this one are the single greatest source of donations to our campaign.

And while I truly wish we did not have to send a single fundraising email, I have no choice with our April fundraising deadline approaching and millions of dollars pouring into Texas to prop up my Republican opponents. The truth is, our fundraising has been slower than we expected this month. With Republicans in a bruising runoff, we have the advantage of a head start — but only if we have the resources to organize and scale up across Texas. Early money has an outsized impact on what is possible. The money we raise today will determine whether or not we can bring people over to our side and turn out new voters who will decide this race in November. Waiting until after the runoff is not an option when billionaire and corporate mega-donors are trying to buy this race. I wish I didn’t have to ask you, but messages like this one are the single greatest source of donations to our campaign. **In one week, ballots for the June 2nd primary will start landing in mailboxes across CA-07 — and when they do, this race enters a completely different phase.**

Voters will start making decisions, conversations will turn into votes, and everything we've built together over these last several months will be put to the test.

The corporate establishment is preparing for this ballot drop too, and they're already spending big to try to lock this race up before voters have a real chance to hear our message. That's how they've always operated — flood the airwaves early, drown out the competition, and coast to the finish line on the strength of their donor rolodex.

We're doing this differently.

This campaign has never taken a dime from corporate PACs, and we never will. What we have instead is something they can't buy — a growing movement of people who believe that CA-07 deserves a real fighter, not more of the same.

**[But keeping that movement moving takes resources, and this next week matters more than any other. Peter,
With just a couple days to go until the end of the month, I’m feeling grateful.
I know you’re likely getting a lot of messages right now, so thank you for opening my email and staying engaged. I appreciate it.

Here’s the thing: We’re up against a crucial April end-of-month deadline, and we still need to reach our $500,000 goal. The momentum is on our side, but if we miss this goal, it could all go to waste.
**It doesn’t look like you’ve chipped in to our campaign yet. I understand – but today, I’m hoping that changes.** Experts say that Democrats have no chance to take back the Senate without winning in North Carolina – and a recent poll shows this race statistically tied.

**The only way I can keep surging ahead and take action against the millions in GOP dark money being thrown our way is if new donors like you join me.**
**[$5 is the most strategic donation you can make right now to help flip the Senate for Democrats and return power to the people. Can I count on you to chip in?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cvf-email-26?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk267-v2&amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=5&t=14&refcode2=1210_124072_Xit6nW&akid=1210%2E124072%2EXit6nW)**

Thank you for everything.

Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

clean_body: God’s children are not for sale—help us prove it She was rescued. Many are still waiting. You can help find them. | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | Peter,A little girl sat alone in the dark. Lured online by someone pretending to care and taken from her home. Kidnapped and hidden away in a remote cabin, where she was abused, and sold online. And passed from one man to another. Her name is Alice. And this is the part most people never hear. She was found. An investigator in Florida traced her trafficker's username. He saw a connection others missed and contacted the FBI. Agents followed the digital trail, tracing the trafficker's IP address. They moved in, raided the location and rescued her. Alive. Her trafficker now faces 20 years to life in prison. This is what happens when someone goes looking. This is what happens when the right tools are in place. But there are still so many children who have not been found yet. Still waiting. Still trapped. And that is why the Sound of Freedom Foundation exists. Peter, if this is your first time hearing about us, the Sound of Freedom Foundation 's mission is clear: To stop the sale of God 's children. The foundation extends the reach of the Sound of Freedom film, bringing awareness to the reality of child trafficking and taking action to stop it. Our vision is simple: A world where every child is safe and free. We work with partners to prevent exploitation before it begins, support rescue operations, and equip investigators. Our partners walk with survivors as they heal and rebuild their lives. Because rescue is only the beginning. And right now, there is an urgent need. We are launching Operation Search and Rescue, a mission to connect investigators and agents, identify traffickers, and build criminal evidence. We will support real rescue operations using tools like digital tracking and face recognition. This is how children are found and how traffickers are stopped. And today, you can be part of it. And right now, your donation will be matched, dollar for dollar.A concerned Child Defense Organization has approved a $10,000 MATCHING GRANT. Every dollar you give will be doubled. $25 Gift Doubles to $50 $50 Gift Doubles to $100 $100 Gift Doubles to $200 $250 Gift Doubles to $500 $500 Gift Doubles to $1,000 Your gift goes twice as far to help find and rescue children. This is God multiplying love. Jesus said, " Whoever welcomes one little child like this in my name welcomes me." (Matthew 18:5) Today you can be that welcome. You can enable the search and help the rescue mission to bring a child home. Please give as generously as you can while your gift is matched. And please pray for Alice, and for the children still waiting. And for the day when every child is safe and free. Because God 's children are not for sale. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074

[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckM1q6zAUhJ9G3sVIR3_OQovLDV4UUgINdCmUo-NYVLaDJdevX9xH6G5gho_h-7z6a0g5zc_3MJFb6-DjEv1IOe9EX8Oy1pHGZSsUaSrb7IGDOXF1gs7P2YsmuogxCGzICWutAi5BNqM7SxWQLNoBCbtgyWhJhmOUqgPCoUnuQHEFHUgNnLfciIdWgYPSwmoDTPGQaa3tSq_tkROGuYZyXEJqcZma7MZaX4XJfwx6Bv2-7-1zOxEu09Ez6OGibqY7fxxRvZm71MdS9mV7CCYv99v_ZnXxtaecUzGWKf6cQsq_9PoHGd8OfgIAAP__qtJq4w)
The Permanent Campaign is brought to you today in partnership with
Republican Task Force Issue: 4/28/2026
King Charles Addresses Congress

King Charles III [delivered a rare address to a joint session of Congress](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDtuwzAQBU9DdTJWK-rjgkUadU6bkliRK5PI6gOSsq8fKLlB6gHmDd7Xwz4oStyen7SySWWxfvc2sMib-XvZUwkc9jOz5zWfm0XAvgZd42g3sU3ljXeeGlexaYZh0AgttlUw84hjT27htr3zgAtppMVpnju-O4C-iuZSgcYR2w4BbtA3c6cJUHfN0PWoNJBwKrfExzlLdLQVyleS45vb10pMKOXIqv1QOCmc6Nj4nS-kcJL4YoVTSed61C5QEs71xf_i62u8SsYf7ygScz8oDc-Vovyqyz-eeBn8CQAA__9DeGwn) on Tuesday afternoon, becoming only the second British monarch in history to do so. Before the speech, Charles met with President Trump in the Oval Office, where Trump declared Americans have ["no closer friends than the British."](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2SgyAURp8GOxy8ApqCYhu7bLulg3Cjd4LgAMbX30n2Dbb-fubM-bnPd0uB4vptdzS5Pmaf_LxhCBfi85Fy3XBLZ0GPeznjDAI0F5LDOMcwd4033nnbuQZNNwyDBNFD32zG-tuCCtViNY5qHF3XDcL5ftAL3PSoGjLvKyFhhF6BEK3Q3aKkFSBVNygNTAobMNc243EugZyN1ZY3ksPWpb0JZqv1KKz_YjAxmK7rauPiIl7lnTOYjhSokisMpprP_eDW7xSp1GwrpchgCvRCvoS0MpieFFfuNpsDFv7XPwt_UaHKXYprxlL4Z3Ae3lYsPLtoewlS6CYbf1wUAhU9MCnW3VL4UNZ_SH0Z-A0AAP__SYeJKg) The visit comes amid strained US-UK relations following the joint US-Israeli war on Iran, with Charles expected to call for "reconciliation and renewal." The address carries real diplomatic stakes: the two countries are actively negotiating a [bilateral trade deal](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDGO5CAURE-DM6zvDwZ3QLCJs950QwvDd4MaG8vQi-b2I88RJqugVPX0_j2Xp40pHq-_didz1W3x2S-BUmpE7y1fNVDIn0Ke9vI5FgRUHCTHaTnSMnTeeOft4Doyg9ZaIggUXTDKT2JDOWihtMCVtALhVm_Xh9gmvY1dNPcUSJxQjAjQgxrWUVpAOQ56VMgk2ERX7S86P2uKzh7VlhvJUe_y3iUTaj0LE38Yzgzn1lp_5hRrdPkuMJwPaiVRrXQVhvOZ7Nea85vhfH8znEHeeWI4h9x4zdyTy554DcTf8XgVXk4iFzjA9JBK6u4y_mwxpViUZhJeu43ph6b-Qt5_g98BAAD__37PfCM) that would be among the first concluded since the Iran war reshuffled global alliances. ★★★
Iran Talks Hit a Wall
